commitAtDiscovery: uncommitted working tree, branch phase-25-m2-verification (Phase 25 / DUR-05/DUR-06 adverse-network DoD verification, PIVOTED per explicit user instruction to root-cause this finding before continuing Phase 25)
oneLineDescription: The SAME 'destIndex outside its own scan window' canary that R0008/R0009 (Phase 20) partially fixed fires AGAIN, on the POST-FIX integrate() (both the Case C rank check from R0008 and the Case B rank check from R0009 present and active), reachable via ordinary, causally-valid but non-FIFO delivery order between exactly 2 replicas -- no duplication needed. Root cause is DIFFERENT IN KIND from R0008/R0009: this is not a bad decision inside one integrate() call's own scan, it is a violation of TRANSITIVITY of relative order across DIFFERENT integrate() calls on different replicas -- two nodes (c and d below) that are NEVER directly rank-compared against each other in any single scan can end up in opposite relative structural order on two replicas, purely as a function of the ORDER in which unrelated intervening nodes were integrated on each replica. When a later operation anchors originLeft to one of that pair and originRight to the other, the receiving replica computes leftIndex > rightIndex - 1 (an INVERTED, negative-width window) and the canary throws immediately, with the for-loop body never executing at all (not a wrong decision inside the scan -- the scan never runs).
harness: A standalone, self-contained, network-free event-script fuzzer built specifically for this investigation (packages/engine/src/_netfuzz.test.ts, scratch, deleted after use): 2-4 real Engine instances; a linear script of MINT events (localInsert 70%/localDelete 30% on a uniformly-chosen replica, immediate-delivery style) and separate DELIVER events (deliver a specific already-minted message, by index, to a specific replica) whose ORDER is independent of mint order -- explicitly modeling exactly what a reordering/duplicating/dropping network relay produces: causally-VALID (ready() still gates every delivery) but FIFO-VIOLATING arrival order per sender. Isolated per fault type: reorder-only (some deliveries jump ahead of earlier-numbered messages), duplicate-only (each delivery may repeat immediately, strict per-sender FIFO otherwise), drop-only (some deliveries never happen; everything is flushed once at the very end). Delta-debugged via greedy single- and pair-event removal plus a mint-kind (delete-to-insert) simplification pass, mirroring R0008's own methodology.

isolationResults.reorder-only: REPRODUCES. Minimal: 2 replicas, 8 mints, 16 total events (8 mint + 8 deliver; 8,000+ other deliveries were redundant flush traffic removed by delta-debugging). See minimalReproduction below.
isolationResults.drop-only: ALSO REPRODUCES, independently, with the IDENTICAL final error signature and structurally the same mechanism (confirmed by hand-trace: drop-only's own 'flush everything at the end' step reintroduces the same FIFO-violating arrival order as reorder-only, just via a different generation path -- dropping early deliveries and catching them up in one late flush IS a form of reordering relative to what arrives promptly). Not treated as a fourth mechanism; see relatedEntries.
isolationResults.duplicate-only (strict per-sender FIFO,: DID NOT REPRODUCE within the search budget (nReplicas 2-4, nMints 3-20, 6000 seeds each). A SEPARATE check -- a plain reconnect/rebuild (rebuildEngineForReconnect's own replay-via-synthetic-inserts mechanism, exactly what CATCHUP mode uses) with ZERO network faults of any kind -- also did not reproduce (nReplicas 2-4, nMints 3-20, 3000 seeds each). CONCLUSION: pure duplication, and a bare reconnect, are each independently insufficient. The original network-relay-level 'duplicate-alone' finding (Test Plan DUR-05/06 verification, this same investigation) went through SyncClient.rebuildEngineForReconnect -> replaySnapshotNodesInto -> applyRemote -> drain -> Engine.integrate, and the diag3.test.ts scenario that produced it forces a FULL DISCONNECT/RECONNECT CYCLE AFTER a burst of live duplicate-faulted traffic, not duplication in isolation. The most likely explanation, NOT YET CONFIRMED BY A REDUCED REPRO: duplicate delivery of an OPS frame during LIVE (pre-reconnect) traffic caused two clients' engines to reach the same kind of transitivity-violating relative order this entry documents (via some path this harness's reorder/drop search didn't happen to sample at these seed/size budgets, since duplicate-only's search space differs from reorder-only's), and the RECONNECT/CATCHUP replay is what turned that latent structural inconsistency into an observable throw (replaying an already-inconsistent node list through a fresh engine is exactly R0008/R0009's own 'replay bakes in whatever structural state already existed' concern). This is an OPEN ITEM -- 'duplicate-alone' is not yet reduced to its own minimal, standalone, network-free fixture, and should not be assumed to be the identical mechanism as this entry's reorder/drop repros until a duplicate-only-plus-reconnect search actually finds one. Do not close this gap by assuming R0010 subsumes it without a confirming repro.

minimalReproduction.description: 2 replicas, engine replica ids 1 and 2 respectively. Exactly 8 real Operations, delivered via applyRemote in the listed order (NOT mint order for the last three deliveries -- that violation of per-sender FIFO order is the entire trigger). msg7 (the 8th operation, minted by replica 2) throws while integrating on replica 1, at the very end.

OUT OF FIFO ORDER relative to msg2/msg4, which replica1 has NOT yet received -- but msg7's own two origins (g, d) ARE both already present on replica1 (both are replica1's own local inserts), so ready() returns true and it integrates IMMEDIATELY, before replica1 has ever heard of 'c' or 'e'. Fast-path (leftIndex=index(g)=0, rightIndex=index(d)=1, empty window): inserted directly. Replica1 structure becomes [g, h, d, f, a-tomb]. NO ERROR YET.

'c' (oL=null, oR=null) finally reaches replica1. Scans the WHOLE structure [g,h,d,f,a-tomb]: at i=0 (g, replica1) compareRank(g,c)<0 (replica1 < replica2) -> destIndex=1, conflicting cleared. At i=1 (h, replica2): h's own originLeft is g, which IS in `scanned` (Case B) but conflicting was just cleared -> compareRank(h,c): both replica2, TIE, not<0 -> BREAK (the R0009 fix's own 'do not blindly inherit' branch). Final destIndex=1. Replica1 structure becomes [g, c, h, d, f, a-tomb] -- 'c' now sits BEFORE 'd', the OPPOSITE of replica2's own view where 'd' has always been before 'c'. NO ERROR YET -- this insertion is entirely valid on its own terms; the inconsistency is silent and structural only, exactly R0008's own 'costs nothing on its own' pattern.

'e' (oL={c:3,r:1}=d, oR={c:3,r:2}=c) finally reaches replica1. ready(): both d and c now present -> ready. integrate(): leftIndex = index(d) = 3 (structure is now [g,c,h,d,f,a-tomb]). rightIndex = index(c) = 1. leftIndex+1=4, rightIndex=1 -- INVERTED. The scan for-loop (`for i=4; i<1; i++`) never executes even once. destIndex stays at its initial value, leftIndex+1=4. Final check: destIndex(4) > rightIndex(1) -> THROWS.

minimalReproduction.exactError: integrate(): computed destIndex 4 for candidate 4:2 outside its own scan window [4, 1] — this is an integrate() bookkeeping bug, unrelated to the retired Engine Spec §6.2 sub-case iii-d claim (see the Case B/Case C comments above).

handTrace.summary: This is NOT a wrong decision inside a single integrate() scan (R0008/R0009's own shape) -- both the Case B and Case C rank checks those fixes added are present, active, and never violated by any INDIVIDUAL comparison in this trace. The bug is that Engine Spec §4.3's origin-bounded placement algorithm, as fixed, guarantees a CORRECT decision only for the specific pair(s) directly rank-compared within one scan -- it provides NO guarantee that the relative order of two nodes NEVER directly compared to each other (here, 'd' and 'c') is the same across two replicas that reached their current structure via DIFFERENT SEQUENCES of intervening insertions. On replica 2, 'd' was placed relative to 'g' (Case C, tie, no advance) and 'c' was placed relative to 'g' at an EARLIER point in time before 'd' or 'h' existed -- 'd' ends up left of 'c' purely as an artifact of insertion timing, not of any rank relationship between d and c themselves (neither op even references the other as an origin). On replica 1, the SAME underlying nodes (g, h, c, d) are integrated in a DIFFERENT order (h arrives and integrates BEFORE c, because msg7 is causally ready via its own origins g/d without needing c or e at all) -- and c, when it finally arrives, gets placed relative to g and h (via Case A/Case B), landing to the LEFT of h, and therefore to the LEFT of d as well, the OPPOSITE of replica 2's own relative order. Neither placement decision individually violates any invariant the current Case A/B/C rank checks enforce; the violation only becomes externally visible when a THIRD operation (e) later needs BOTH d and c as its own two origins and discovers their relative order has silently inverted between replicas.
handTrace.whyThisIsNotR0008OrR0009: R0008: a Case C node was unconditionally skipped (blind break) regardless of its own rank vs the candidate -- fixed by adding a direct rank check. R0009: a Case B node blindly inherited its anchor's own resolution without its OWN rank vs the candidate being consulted -- fixed by adding a direct rank check there too. In THIS trace, replay every single Case A/B/C decision made (msg2 vs g: Case A, rank check correctly applied; msg2 vs h: Case B, rank check correctly applied, correctly does NOT inherit and correctly breaks; msg7 vs the fast path; msg5/msg6 vs their own windows) -- none of them is wrong by the POST-FIX rules. The bug is one level ABOVE any single scan: it is that the ALGORITHM'S OWN CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT (Case A/B/C's per-scan rank comparisons, taken together, are supposed to induce ONE global total order that every replica converges to regardless of delivery order) does not actually hold once a node (h) can become causally ready and integrate into a position relative to g/d WITHOUT ever having been compared against a node (c) that a DIFFERENT, not-yet-arrived operation will later need to relate to both g/d and h/c as a single consistent order. This is a genuinely NEW, THIRD mechanism -- not a residual gap in either R0008 or R0009's specific fix, but evidence that the origin-bounded scan's local pairwise correctness does not compose into global order consistency under non-FIFO (but still fully causally-valid, ready()-respecting) delivery.
handTrace.keyStructuralObservation: The failure signature itself (destIndex > rightIndex, with leftIndex+1 > rightIndex, i.e. a WHOLLY INVERTED, negative-width window where the for-loop body never runs at all) is structurally distinguishable from R0008/R0009's own failure shape (destIndex landing one step past a VALID, positive-width window because of one wrong in-scan decision). Any future investigation of this canary should check leftIndex vs rightIndex BEFORE assuming it's the same R0008/R0009 gap: leftIndex > rightIndex-1 means the two origins named by the arriving operation are ALREADY in the wrong relative order on this replica before the scan even begins -- the scan logic is not the place to look for the bug; the place to look is why 'd' and 'c' (or whatever the two origins are) ended up in opposite relative order on the two replicas in the first place.

convergenceImpact.conclusion: OPEN. Given R0008's own precedent (a structurally-divergent-but-text-convergent state was later shown to produce real visible-text divergence via one more anchoring operation), and given this entry's mechanism is a strict superset in severity (it doesn't even reach 'text matches, structure differs' quietly -- it throws outright, which in a real deployment with the canary compiled out or the exception swallowed by a generic catch-all would very plausibly leave the operation silently dropped, exactly matching the real network-relay finding's own observed symptom: 'server.ts's generic top-level catch-all (ws.messageHandlerFailed), silently dropping the message'), a real visible-text divergence following the same shape as R0008's followUpOperationImpact is considered LIKELY but UNCONFIRMED.

productionReachability: CONFIRMED reachable through real, non-test-only code paths, independent of this harness: the original finding (Test Plan DUR-05/06 adverse-network DoD verification, this same investigation, prior to reduction to this engine-only fixture) reproduced the IDENTICAL canary message shape through three real product code paths: (1) SyncClient.handleOps, live editing, delay+reorder network conditions, no reconnect involved; (2) the server's own coordinator.engine, inside writePath.ts's unguarded applyRemote call in the apply loop, under delay+drop network conditions -- caught only by gateway.ts's generic top-level catch-all (ws.messageHandlerFailed), silently dropping the message; (3) SyncClient.rebuildEngineForReconnect -> replaySnapshotNodesInto, under duplicate-alone network conditions with a forced reconnect. This engine-only fixture (R0010) is the network-free, minimal, Rule-3-compliant reduction of finding (1) specifically (delay+reorder-alone) and is confirmed (via the drop-only isolation above) to also explain finding (2); finding (3) remains an open item, see isolationResults above.
relatedEntriesNote: Same canary assertion (the Phase 20 structural sanity check, 'destIndex outside its own scan window'), same file, but a THIRD, independent, genuinely NEW mechanism -- confirmed via hand-trace against the ACTUAL post-R0008/R0009-fix integrate() code (both rank checks present and correctly applied throughout this trace; neither is what fails). This is not evidence the R0008/R0009 fix is incomplete in the sense of 'missed a case within one scan' -- every individual scan decision in this trace is correct under the current rules. It IS evidence that the origin-bounded scan design's local correctness does not compose into a globally consistent total order under non-FIFO delivery, which is a materially different and more fundamental class of finding than either prior entry.
status: FIXED (2026-09-05). Given this was the THIRD distinct bug found in the same Case A/B/C decision procedure (R0008, R0009, now R0010), each discovered under a new test condition after the previous fix, the decision was made to REPLACE the algorithm outright rather than patch it a third time -- the pattern itself was treated as evidence the local, per-branch rank-check approximation (this project's own Phase 3 derivation, refined at R0008/R0009) is structurally unsound for transitivity, not merely incomplete in one more spot. `Engine.integrate()` was rewritten as a faithful port of the real, PUBLISHED, peer-reviewed YATA algorithm (Kleppmann, 'Near Real-Time Peer-to-Peer Shared Editing on Extensible Data Types'; reference implementation verified against source: Sypytkowski, https://github.com/Horusiath/crdt-examples/blob/master/Crdt/convergent/Yata.fs) -- see engine.ts's own integrate() doc comment for the full algorithm text and the CLAUDE.md 'Engine Spec §4.3 replaced by the real YATA algorithm (R0010)' entry for the complete investigation. Key finding during verification: the real algorithm's Case-C-equivalent branch (`otherLeftIndex < leftIndex`) is an UNCONDITIONAL stop with NO rank check at all -- the opposite of what R0008's own patch added -- and its Case-B-equivalent uses a single carried-forward `scanning` boolean (not this project's own former `scanned`/`conflicting` Sets), which is what actually supplies transitive consistency across separate integrate() calls. A real off-by-one WAS found and fixed during this port's own verification (not by review): a `for` loop bounded by `i < rightIndex` misses the reference algorithm's own final `dst` re-derivation at `i === rightIndex`, which silently reproduced RFC NQ-2's exact 'zcybxa' interleaving bug on the very first run against engine.test.ts's own §10.7 worked trace -- fixed by translating the recursion as a literal `while(true)` loop with an explicit exit check, matching the reference algorithm exactly. FULL VERIFICATION, all against the real, merged engine.ts: R0008 (all 6 causally-valid delivery-order permutations converge to 'it'), R0009 (all 3 causally-valid delivery-order permutations converge to 'itp'), R0010 (out-of-FIFO delivery converges to the identical text AND structure as natural in-order delivery, 'ghdfec') -- all three exhaustively re-verified against the real file, not just the pre-implementation scratch port. `pnpm test` (engine package, 59/59, including the corrected §10.7 trace); full monorepo default `pnpm test` (425/425 across 45 files); `pnpm test:adversarial` (22/22); `pnpm test:properties` (6/6 suites, 10,000 cases each); `pnpm test:index` (10,000-seed PositionIndex cross-check vs. a linear-scan oracle, zero disagreements); `pnpm test:convergence` (ALL SEVEN configs at the full 10,000-seed budget each, 70,000/70,000 converged, ZERO divergences -- including C7-immediate-delivery, the exact config that found R0008/R0009 at 22-95% failure rates pre-fix, now clean); `pnpm test:mutation` (10 of 10 mutants killed -- a STRONGER result than the pre-fix baseline, where M3_no_case_c survived every suite by design; the real-YATA-port's Case-C-equivalent branch is now caught by the ordinary pure-convergence fuzzer at seed 0, meaning it no longer needs the specialized MUT-KILL-01 10^6-trial search to detect at all -- two of the ten mutants' find/replace anchors needed mechanical updates for the new engine.ts source shape: M3_no_case_c's own anchor, and M8_no_idempotence's anchor, the latter a genuinely PRE-EXISTING gap from Phase 21's applyRemote() context-parameter addition, unrelated to this fix, surfaced only by actually re-running this gate). `tests/regression/R0008` and `R0009` are updated with cross-references to this correction; all three entries remain permanently retained per Test Plan §2.3 Rule 2.
